gpu_accounting.benchmark_body_span_definition: The source starts its internal timer after CPU select_accepted and torch import, before CUDA tensor creation; this span includes construction/JIT, GPU qualification and warmed timing, but excludes CPU selection/import and process teardown. It is distinct from supervisor reservation and CUDA-event medians.
gpu_accounting.definition: Single GPU reserved through CPU selection, first kernel construction/JIT, GPU qualification, warmed timing and complete worker exit; excludes preceding CPU-only deploy checks.

allocation_policy: each call allocates both gather and scatter outputs; same lifecycle for torch and Triton
scope: same fixed held selections; synthetic native-stride BF16 Q and token-major output

qualification: Exact gather, scatter, and inverse equality against Torch before any timed use.
interpretation: A standalone permutation negative; do not add these times to a different-host consumer result or infer attention/request/quality performance.
timing_semantics: CUDA events surround Python component calls and may include GPU waiting gaps from host dispatch. This is current component-call cost, not isolated device-kernel bandwidth or duration. Oracle/D2H validation does not repeat in timed calls. Additional Triton Python checks/launcher contribution is unmeasured; the entire gap cannot be attributed to it.
